chapter: Queens Terrace, Decca records and Amen
title: Swampland, Bingie Madison and the Tampa Boys
summary: Swampland was written by Bingie Madison; Don Stovall sang; the Tampa Boys only sat in.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Because he would have had--Well, Swampland was Bingie's tune, Bingie Madison; I know that.
Did Bingie write that?
Bingie wrote that.
Some other guy wrote the words.
You're the only one who ever made a record of that, as far as I know.
Did you ever hear that record?
No.
Oh, that's beautiful.
I don't know who sang it.
Don Stovall; that's on the other side of "Amen".
Right; right.
Did you ever hear that?
No.
You ought to hear that.
Why are The Tampa Boys
They weren't working with me, they just asked me to let them do a number with me.
Where were you at this time? Where were you working? Were you at the Sunnyside--the Horseshoe Bar at this time?
I had just left the Horseshoe Bar, but I still had the same band recording with me, that was playing with me at the Sunnyside Bar.
Stovall and all those guys.
They were with me at the Sunnyside.
